messages:
Ellie Park: Quick flag  I ran a spot-check of recent hires and found ~5 interviews where the scorecard fields are filled but the calibrated rubric wasn't used (freeform notes only). That makes calibration metrics noisy. Can we add an automated gate that warns interviewers if they try to submit without selecting the calibrated template?

Tom Rivers: Agreed. We should do a soft-block: show a modal that says 'You haven't selected the calibrated rubric for this role. Select it to continue or confirm you understand the guidance.' Put an option 'I confirm' that logs the override. That gives visibility without hard-blocking.
Marissa Lee: Love the override + audit trail idea. Also suggest a nightly job that validates all completed interviews and emits a CSV for hiring managers showing overrides + missing templates. That helps measure drift.
Emily (People Ops): Sounds actionable. Quick implementation plan: 1) UX modal + override checkbox (frontend) 2) API validation to return 409 if template missing (soft validation codepath) 3) nightly validator job to produce CSV and create ticket if count > 0. I can draft copy for the modal and the email to interviewers.

Tom Rivers: For the API side I can add a flag 'allow_override=true' that frontend sets when user confirms. We'll log override_user and override_reason. Backend will still accept submission but emit a metric 'scorecard.override' with counts.

Ellie Park: Can we also add a lightweight pre-submit client check in mobile app to prevent the common mobile issue where template dropdown resets? A small UX tweak there will cut down on mobile-related misses.

Marissa Lee: Yep, Mobile team needs a ticket. I'll file a short JIRA with acceptance criteria: ensure template selection is persisted across the flow and include an explicit confirmation step for overrides.

Ops Bot: Feature ticket created: INT-4892 (scorecard-rubric-guardrails). Nightly job ticket: INT-4893 (scorecard-nightly-validator). Mobile ticket: MBL-221.

Emily (People Ops): Draft modal copy: 'Redwood calibrated rubric recommended for this role. Using it keeps ratings consistent across interviews. Select "Use calibrated rubric" or check "I understand and will justify" to proceed. Frequent overrides will trigger follow-up training.' Thoughts?

Tom Rivers: Clean. Add a small link to a one-page guide: /hiring/toolkit/calibrated-rubric. Also include a tooltip on the override explaining examples of acceptable reasons.

Ellie Park: One more ask: can the nightly validator produce a short leaderboard for teams showing % use of calibrated rubric? That gives managers a quick health signal.

Marissa Lee: Yes  we'll include team, role, interviewer_id, interviews_done, overrides, pct_calibrated. I'll wire it into the hiring metrics dashboard.

Emily (People Ops): I'll coordinate comms and schedule a 20-minute micro-training next week for top interviewers. Two slots: Tue 16:00 UTC and Thu 09:30 UTC. RSVP link to follow.

Tom Rivers: I'll scope the backend changes and aim to land the API flag + metric this sprint. Est ETA: 5 days.

Ellie Park: Thanks team. Small changes but should improve signal a lot. Closing loop when tickets land. :white_check_mark:
